messages.subject: slicing of matrix
parts:
I have a matrix of predictor variables its measurement errors
            matrix[n, k] x;
            matrix[n, k] errx;

and parameters
          matrix[n, k] xtrue;

and would like to define in a model the following:
           x ~ normal(xtrue, errx)

but this fails because x is a matrix. The only way I cae n get this to work is to slice
the array using the row function.

                for (i in 1:k) row(x, i) ~ normal(row(x, i), row(errx, i));
I would expect that I need to use the col function to loop through
the k columns in the matrix but that fails. Why one needs to use row and
there is any other way to define this model?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] slicing of matrix
parts: I don't understand what you're trying to do, but see below.

> On Oct 21, 2015, at 8:24 PM, Miguel de Val-Borro <miguel...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I have a matrix of predictor variables its measurement errors
> matrix[n, k] x;
> matrix[n, k] errx;
>

> and would like to define in a model the followinge
> x ~ normal(x, errx)


? x is both the outcome and the mean ? That's the same as 0 ~ normal(0, errx).

> but this fails because x is a matrix. The only way I cae n get this to work is to slice
> the array using the row function.
>
> for (i in 1:k) row(x, i) ~ normal(row(x, i), row(errx, i));
> I would expect that I need to use the col function to loop through
> the k columns in the matrix but that fails. Why one needs to use row and
> there is any other way to define this model?

There's also something wrong in the above in that you let i run from 1:k,
but the matrix is (n x k), so it has n rows, not k rows.

There's a chapter in the manual on arrays vs. matrices with efficiency
concerns. For this, you can do something like this:

to_vector(x) ~ normal(to_vector(y???), to_vector(err_x))

which will flatten things out. Instead of row(x, i), you can use x[i], but it's
even better then to make x an array of vectors --- no copying that way.

We haven't yet implemented vectorization that takes parallel matrices.

- Bob
